bullets.title: NVDA: $100B+ OpenAI Ohio campus deal confirmed, $1.5B SB Energy investment
bullets.body: NVIDIA confirmed as exclusive AI compute provider for SB Energy's PORTS-Pike Technology Campus in Ohio under a 20-year lease, providing 8 IT-GW systems to OpenAI. NVDA will invest $1.5B in SB Energy and offer credit support for an initial 4.25 IT-GW with option for 3.75 GW more; OpenAI's total compute commitments through 2030 represent ~$600B of NVIDIA revenue. NVDA also invests $4.2B jointly with SB Energy to develop 10 GW of energy infrastructure, while NVDA bullish options flow is the strongest of any stock today with $7M+ in short-dated OTM calls.

bullets.title: SNDK: +42% in 4 days on massive unusual call activity
bullets.body: SanDisk surged another 10% intraday Monday, bringing the 4-day gain to +42.1%. Unusual million-dollar call prints flagged; HFTs reportedly exploiting the volatile name by widening bid-ask spreads on odd-lot trades.

bullets.title: MU: Stock crosses $1,000, +15% in one month; $7M+ bullish options flow
bullets.body: Micron traded above $1,000/share (+15% in a month). Large $7M+ short-dated OTM calls were flagged jointly with NVDA as semiconductors see unusually bullish flow. Micron's Chief Business Officer Sumit Sadana confirmed as speaker at TomorrowX Summit with focus on how AI is changing memory business models.

bullets.title: AMZN: Morgan Stanley targets $500 by end-2027; Anthropic stake valued at $190B+
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley set a $500 price target for Amazon by end-2027, with the bull case hinging on AWS reaching $1T annual revenue driven by AI compute demand. Separately, Amazon's stake in Anthropic is now estimated to be worth more than $190B.

bullets.title: AMAT: Approaching first-ever $10B+ revenue quarter with 50%+ YoY Q4 growth
bullets.body: Applied Materials is tracking toward its first-ever $10B+ revenue quarter, with Q4 guidance implying more than 50% YoY growth at midpoint. China is returning to growth and ICAPS recovery is underway, though the stock sold off despite earnings strength—reverse DCF analysis suggests the market may be undervaluing the setup.

bullets.title: AMD: $800M capex spend signals fabless model blurring
bullets.body: AMD is spending $800M in capex vs. the historical $200-300M range for a fabless designer, suggesting the company is securing scarce substrates and memory supply directly rather than relying on foundry partners. AIDA64 also added AMD Zen 7 server support nearly two years ahead of EPYC Florence's expected launch.

bullets.title: MRVL: UBS cuts PT to $300 from $340
bullets.body: UBS trimmed its Marvell Technology price target from $340 to $300, implying a ~12% reduction to the prior target level. No rating change noted.

bullets.title: META: Sentiment overly negative despite strong core business and AI tailwinds
bullets.body: One analyst argued META sentiment is 'extremely negative' despite one of the strongest and stickiest core businesses in big tech. Recent quarterly results showed positive AI/GenAI integration driving engagement and ad targeting improvements. Separately, an investor disclosed a new purchase of META shares.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Now Berkshire Hathaway's 3rd-largest holding
bullets.body: Google is now Berkshire Hathaway's third-largest holding per recent disclosures. The stock was also flagged in a weekly research note citing capacity constraints and 'brain drain' as risk factors.

bullets.title: TTD vs APP: Management style contrasted — Green blames others, Foroughi owns issues
bullets.body: LightShed drew a sharp contrast between AppLovin's Adam Foroughi (takes ownership of operational issues) and Trade Desk's Jeff Green (attributes problems to external factors), suggesting better accountability culture at APP.

bullets.title: COHR/LITE: 1.6T optical timeline delays could be tailwind; OCP APAC takeaways
bullets.body: A research note from OCP APAC Summit flagged scale-up networking transitioning from copper to optics; analyst noted 1.6T timeline delays would favor LITE and COHR if 6-inch to next-gen wafer transition slips. Attach rates expected to be 'very low and slow' per one skeptic.

bullets.title: UBER: Partners with Zipline targeting 1M daily drone deliveries
bullets.body: Uber and Zipline announced a drone delivery partnership with the stated goal of achieving 1 million drone deliveries per day. Delivery target for sub-10-lb packages; one prominent investor called it a 'big deal.'

bullets.title: TSLA: Bulls ignoring valuation per Gary Black; Model Y pricing economics debated
bullets.body: Gary Black warned Tesla bulls are 'loving the product' but ignoring valuation. Separately, a debate emerged over Model Y production costs (~$35K) vs. Elon's pricing claims. One analyst argued P/E to forward EPS growth is the right valuation framework to capture future product economics.

bullets.title: INTC/NVDA: Millions in call option prints flagged; Intel Nova Lake targets desktops first
bullets.body: Options flow trackers flagged millions in call prints across INTC and NVDA. On the product side, Intel's Nova Lake chip is reportedly targeting desktops before servers—a strategic reversal vs. AMD's server-first Zen 6/EPYC Venice approach.

bullets.title: AAPL: German regulator accuses Apple of anti-competitive pop-up design
bullets.body: A German regulator accused Apple of designing app permission pop-ups in a way that favors its own apps over third-party rivals, potentially disadvantaging third-party app developers.

bullets.title: Big Tech AI capex: $3T in off-balance-sheet commitments vs. $600B reported
bullets.body: Analysis flagged that nine major tech companies have approximately $3 trillion in off-balance-sheet AI commitments vs. only $600B in reported capex, leaving $2.4T in unrecognized obligations. The AI arms race is creating enormous financial obligations not fully captured on balance sheets.

bullets.title: AMAT/NBIS/SMCI/GOOGL: Weekly semi note flags capacity constraints, memory ASP normalization
bullets.body: A weekly research note flagged capacity constraints across the semiconductor chain, described memory ASP normalization as 'healthy,' cited Google consolidation and brain drain concerns, and flagged LITE, COHR, NBIS, AMD, and SMCI for upcoming product days.

bullets.title: Oil surges: Brent above $90, WTI at $84 on Hormuz crisis; refiner stocks grinding higher
bullets.body: Brent crude climbed ~3% above $90/barrel and WTI rose to $84.14 as Iran seized a UAE-owned tanker in the Strait of Hormuz and Hormuz crossings reportedly returned to zero. Refiners VLO, MPC, PSX, and DINO continue grinding higher with no fundamental impact from recent jawboning; diesel crack spreads approaching $100, framed as the real Hormuz hedge.

bullets.title: Macro: 30Y Treasury hits 5.30% (2007 high); Wells Fargo flips to two rate hikes by 2027
bullets.body: The 30-year Treasury yield reached 5.29–5.30%, the highest since the 2007 pre-GFC period, with Citadel Securities attributing the move to Fed policy risk. Wells Fargo Investment Institute reversed its prior no-change forecast, now expecting +25bps hikes in both 2026 and 2027, lifting fed funds to 4.00–4.25%. Goldman still sees September hike as 'very unlikely.' Evercore ISI's Julian Emanuel targets S&P 500 at 9,000 within 12 months.
